issues.failure_explanation: The bound is asserted with a constant C(ρ,p) independent of f_v (or u0), but the target function can be scaled by an arbitrary constant through u0, scaling the approximation error. The paper elsewhere bounds ||f_v|| by B(u0,T,M), but this factor is missing in Cor cor:LS and in the supporting Theorem th:main_ls.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply the bound by B(u0,T,M) (or by ||f_v||_{L∞(Eρ)}) in Cor cor:LS and add the analogous norm factor in Theorem th:main_ls.
issues.overall_effect: The least-squares convergence guarantee is not scale-invariant and is false as stated for large u0; the proof cannot establish the stated bound without adding the missing norm factor.
issues.title: Least-squares error bound omits target norm factor
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local missing multiplicative factor; the rate and scope survive without new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follow directly from  \cite[Theorem~7.12]{sparsepoly} and Theorem \ref{thm:mainthm}.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited compressed-sensing theorem requires the hyperbolic cross index set to have cardinality controlled by the sample-derived quantity \tilde{m}. Setting the order n = ceil(\tilde{m}) makes |\Lambda_{n-1}^{HC}| potentially much larger than \tilde{m} (e.g., in higher dimensions the cardinality estimate can exceed \tilde{m} by orders of magnitude), so the hypotheses of the invoked theorem are not met.

failure_location.quote: $\Lambda = \Lambda_{n-1}^{HC}$ be the hyperbolic cross index set defined in \eqref{eq:HC} with $n = \lceil \tilde{m} \rceil$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose n (depending on \tilde{m} and d) so that |\Lambda_{n-1}^{HC}| ≤ \tilde{m}, e.g., the largest such integer, as in the cited theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The compressed-sensing convergence guarantee for the stated choice of Λ is unsupported; the algorithm as described may use a dictionary too large for the sample size.
issues.title: Compressed-sensing index set order set equal to sample-derived sparsity level
issues.why_classification: The error is in the parameter selection for the index set; fixing it requires replacing n = ceil(\tilde{m}) with a cardinality-based choice, a contained but substantive correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof introduces an integral over [-1,1]^N with Lebesgue measure, which is not defined (infinite-dimensional Lebesgue measure does not exist). It also uses dx rather than the orthogonality measure ϱ. The argument does not validly prove that coefficients with indices outside the first d coordinates vanish.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the infinite-dimensional integral argument with a standard finite-dimensional orthogonality argument: since f depends only on x_1,...,x_d, its coefficients for multi-indices with any ν_k>0 for k>d vanish in the tensor-product basis.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem th:main_ls is invalid, so the supporting result for Cor cor:LS is not established as written.
issues.title: Infinite-dimensional Lebesgue integral in proof of finite-dimensional LS theorem
issues.why_classification: The theorem is standard and the repair is a short local orthogonality argument; the conclusion and downstream rates survive.
